chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hakam, who said:

I said to a slave of ours, 'Prepare lunch for us.' So he took birds from the Haram, slaughtered them, and cooked them. So I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Bury them, and pay the expiation for each of these birds.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca or Medina), a sacred area with specific rules

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for slaughtering birds within the Haram sanctuary?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of expiation (kaffarah) for hunting within the Haram boundaries, specifically highlighting the dual requirement of burying the carcass and paying fidya for each bird. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the sacred precincts by ensuring that the act of consumption does not negate the spiritual violation incurred. The detailed chain of transmission underscores the reliability of this ruling within the Usuli tradition.
